Joint Committee on Transportation Andrew Blunt, Sierra Club Maine April 11, 2025 Testimony in Support of L.D. 1242: An Act to Incentivize the Construction of Solar Carport Canopies and Solar Chargers at Highway Picnic Areas

Senator Nangle, Representative Crafts, and members of the Joint Committee on Transportation,

I write on behalf of Sierra Club Maine, representing over 22,000 supporters and members statewide. Founded in 1892, Sierra Club is one of our nation's oldest and largest environmental organizations. We work diligently to amplify the power of our 3.8 million members nationwide as we work towards combating climate change and promoting a just and sustainable economy. To that end, we urge you to vote "Ought to Pass" on L.D. 1242.

This bill directs the Department of Transportation to enter into no-cost leases for the installation of solar-powered electric vehicle (EV) charging stations at all highway picnic areas. The bill also allows a person who builds a solar carport canopy housing at least two EV charging stations to amortize the sales and use tax assessed on materials and equipment used to construct the canopy and any EV charging stations under it.

Expanding our EV charging network is a critical piece of our state's electrification journey. Transportation continues to be Maine's largest source of carbon emissions, much of which is from light duty passenger vehicle transportation. Therefore, EV adoption by average consumers across Maine must be a top climate priority. There are various barriers to adoption that stop Mainers from making the switch to an EV, but perhaps the most common is limited access to EV charging infrastructure.

This bill leverages publicly-owned land to improve access to EV charging statewide. Even better, it encourages load-neutral chargers powered by co-located solar arrays. This is precisely the type of creative public policy needed to accelerate the rate of beneficial electrification in Maine. We strongly encourage you to vote "Ought to Pass" on L.D. 1242.

Sincerely,

Andrew Blunt Sierra Club Maine Chapter Legislative and Political Strategist

The Nature Conservancy (TNC) is a nonprofit organization dedicated to conserving the lands and waters on which all life depends.
Our organizations support efforts to reduce greenhouse gas emissions across all sectors of our state, and advocate for recommendations and strategies to accomplish this that are laid out in Maine Won't Wait, the state's climate action plan.1 This includes efforts to decarbonize the transportation sector, which is responsible for the largest share of emissions in Maine.2
LD 1242 seeks to encourage the development of solar carport canopies and electric vehicle (EV) charging stations, which we support for several reasons:
1. Solar that is sited alongside load and in already developed areas helps get renewable energy onto the grid with minimal impact.

Generation sited alongside load (like solar panels co-located with the EV charger), is an efficient way to build and use renewable energy as it minimizes the need to build costly transmission infrastructure. Additionally, an electric vehicle powered with sunshine is significantly preferred to an electric vehicle powered with a mix of whatever is on the ISO-NE grid at that moment (which could include natural gas, nuclear, hydro, and others).3 To meet our state climate goals we need to electrify everything (including transportation), and power that electricity with renewable sources of generation. LD 1242 is a small by meaningful step towards doing both at once.

TESTIMONY OF MICHAEL J. ALLEN, ASSOCIATE COMMISSIONER FOR TAX POLICY
DEPARTMENT OF ADMINISTRATIVE AND FINANCIAL SERVICES
Before the Joint Standing Committee on Transportation Hearing Date: April 11, 2025, Friday at 10:00 A.M.
LD 1242 - "An Act to Incentivize the Construction of Solar Carport Canopies and Solar Chargers at Highway Picnic Areas"
Senator Nangle, Representative Crafts, and members of the Transportation Committee - good morning, my name is Michael Allen, Associate Commissioner for Tax Policy in the Department of Administrative and Financial Services. I am testifying at the request of the Administration Against LD 1242, "An Act to Incentivize the Construction of Solar Carport Canopies and Solar Chargers at Highway Picnic Areas."
The bill would allow a person that constructs or has constructed a solar carport canopy to amortize the sales and use tax on materials and equipment purchased to construct the solar carport canopy, and any electric vehicle charging station underneath, annually over a period of 10 years.
The proposal is inconsistent with the workings of the Maine sales and use tax in which the sales tax is imposed on the purchaser and collected by the retailer. It is unclear how the 10-year amortization would work within this framework and the bill does not provide the necessary direction. Further, the effective date of January 1, 2026, does not provide Maine Revenue Services with enough time to determine those details through rulemaking.

Good morning, Chair Nangle, Chair Crafts, and respected colleagues of the Joint Standing Committee on Transportation. I appreciate the opportunity to testify in support of L.D. 1242, An Act to Incentivize the Construction of Solar Carport Canopies and Solar Chargers at Highway Picnic Areas.
When Representative Golek asked me to cosponsor LD 1242, I was more than happy to do so. Learning more about the reasons that this bill represents a positive and equitable step in our efforts to fight climate change make me proud to cosponsor and led me to want to speak to you in support to offer further support in what this bill could represent.
LD 1242 is not only good for the environment and the economy, but it also speaks to the values of accessibility and equity. As EV adoption grows, ensuring access to reliable charging infrastructure in all parts of the state, not just in urban centers, is critical. Highway picnic areas are strategically located and highly visible, making them ideal for this kind of development. This bill ensures that Maine's shift toward clean transportation is inclusive, well-planned, and accessible to residents and tourists alike. By passing LD 1242, the legislature can help build a cleaner, more connected Maine for generations to come.
These charging stations, powered by solar energy, would allow EV drivers to travel across the state with greater confidence in light of `range anxiety' concerns, which is a fact we should not under appreciate. In acknowledgement of our ambitious climate goals, it is these kinds of proactive investments and thinking that can encourage EV adoption by addressing the highly practical concerns faced by some at the prospect of electric over internal combustion vehicles, making this bill's proposal both urgent and commendable.
By directing the Department of Transportation to offer no-cost leases at highway picnic areas for the installation of solar-powered EV charging stations, the bill encourages public-private partnerships that bring essential electric vehicle infrastructure to highly public, easily accessible, and also particularly more rural and underserved areas. The bill's provision allowing businesses and individuals to forgive the sales and use tax on materials used to build solar canopies and EV chargers is a smart economic incentive. This tax relief acknowledges the upfront costs involved in

clean energy projects and offers a realistic pathway for more stakeholders, especially small businesses and local developers, to invest in renewable infrastructure. Rather than providing direct subsidies, which can be fiscally challenging, particularly in the current economic realities, this measure offers long-term financial feasibility while boosting private investment in sustainable energy solutions.
The inclusion of solar carport canopies further amplifies the benefits of this bill. These canopies not only provide renewable energy for electric vehicles but also offer practical advantages such as shelter from sun and snow, important considerations in a state like Maine. The dual functionality of these structures maximizes the utility of public spaces, particularly picnic areas, which already serve as rest and recreation spaces for the public. Encouraging the construction of solar canopies supports clean energy jobs, provides needed infrastructure, and helps integrate sustainability into the everyday travel experience.
LD 1242 promotes environmental and economic benefits while emphasizing accessibility and equity. This strategic development supports Maine's transition to sustainable travel inclusively and visibly, while doing so in an economically sound way. By placing EV charging stations at highway picnic areas across the state, the bill ensures that clean transportation infrastructure reaches both urban and rural areas while also addressing the critical concerns of range anxiety.
Thank you for your time and consideration this testimony and of Rep. Golek's bill.
Scarborough: District 124
